points: The upcoming Q4 2026 earnings call should show whether the promised H2 2026 margin recovery actually materialized, and if it did not, the bull case for a profitability rebound will weaken.
If the call reveals 2026 AI recurring revenue is still short of the $120M threshold, the AI margin-upside story could lose credibility and leave investors with just the core outsourcing business.
Offshoring cost pressure could keep the revenue drain above 200bps into 2027, which would continue to eat into margins and make cost-cutting targets harder to hit.
With debt-to-equity likely staying above 0.5, debt repayment will probably keep soaking up cash that could otherwise go to growth or buybacks, keeping balance-sheet risk in the foreground.

After FY2025 delivered $807M in operating cash flow and $626M in adjusted free cash flow, any drop in 2026 cash generation would slow debt paydown and strengthen the leverage concerns behind the short.
The $258M returned to shareholders in FY2025 looks less sustainable if margins stay under pressure, because management may need to preserve cash for debt and restructuring.

Client concentration and vertical exposure could turn into a liability if a few large clients pull back spending; any revenue-guidance cut on the Q4 2026 call would confirm that FY2025's 4.3% growth is not repeating.
The sector is leaning short and peer VRRM reports on November 4, 2026, so a soft read across the outsourcing group could add selling pressure around CNXC before year-end.
